paper_metadata.title: Dual multi-phase intermetallic alloys composed of geometrically close packed Ni3X (X: Al, Ti and V) type structures – II. Mechanical properties

evidence.quote: The mechanical data of novel alloys based on the pseudo-ternary system Ni 3Al–Ni3Ti–Ni3V was assessed. This alloy system exhibits dual multi-phase microstructures

The high-temperature mechanical properties of the intermetallic alloys based on the Ni3Al–Ni3Ti–Ni3V pseudo-ternary alloy system were investigated, focusing on the low Ti content region where the dual multi-phase microstructures are developed.
Using arc-melted and hot-forged materials, the following results were obtained from the present study.
A significant tensile ductility was observed for hot-forged materials doped with boron. Intergranular fracture was observed over a wide temperature range.

It should be noted that the yield stress of the alloys with dual multi-phase microstructures (Fig. 3 (b)) is significantly higher than that of alloys with the ''lower'' multi-phase microstructure (Fig. 3 (a)). This result suggests that the dual multi-phase microstructure is very useful to strengthen the multi-phase intermetallic alloys.

The present dual multi-phase intermetallic alloys, which are composed of L12 and D022 phases (or L12, D022 and D024 phases), exhibit a yield strength anomaly, as shown in Figs. 3–8. This result is closely related to the fact that alloys Ni3Al (L12), Ni3V (D022) and Ni3Ti (D024) display the positive temperature dependence of the flow (or yield) strength.
